medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness and protective prescription
medicines.dose: Prescribed and reconciled by the specialist team
medicines.timing: The prescription specifies treatment-day, delayed and rescue support

additional_support: Cisplatin has high nausea/vomiting risk. Agree prevention and rescue anti-sickness medicines, prescribed hydration and electrolyte replacement. A separate white-cell growth-factor plan may be chosen for clinical need. Do not add diuretics or change fluid intake yourself.

Bring the full medicine list, report infection or hearing/nerve changes, and confirm the anti-sickness and hydration prescription. Discuss heart history, all prior anthracyclines, fertility and the surgery plan.

The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Never change pump settings or disconnect an infusion yourself.

local_reference.label: CUH Department of Medical Oncology: Adjuvant medication prescription for chemotherapy High Risk for nausea and vomiting, Version 2 (05/05/2021)
local_reference.note: Complete historical CUH reference for reconciliation, not an issued prescription. Preserve one individual treatment-day, delayed and rescue plan. Do not automatically repeat a start-day course, combine competing courses, or transfer fixed adult reference doses to a child. The treating team confirms each item, actual days, interactions and duration. The days2–3 active-agent moderate label does not stop or downgrade delayed-emesis coverage after day1 cisplatin. Reconcile this multiday course as one prescription. The local CUH source is retained as a reference list, not as the national antiemetic standard. Nystatin/chlorhexidine are displayed as local mouth-care adjuncts, not universal antiemetic or mucositis prophylaxis. Verify current local oral-care policy. Inherited reference safety notes: Caution: metoclopramide with olanzapine may increase extrapyramidal adverse effects. Dexamethasone may be modified or omitted where the systemic anticancer therapy regimen already includes a steroid. Metoclopramide: adult maximum 10 mg up to three times daily (30 mg/day) and maximum treatment duration 5 days under current European/Irish product information; avoid prolonged repeated use without review.

Six full cycles give a planned doxorubicin total of 450 mg/m²; the source also states a 450 mg/m² lifetime ceiling. Prior anthracyclines and cardiac risk may lower the allowable individual exposure.

clinical_source_boundaries: Age ≤40; source anatomical exclusions and complete resectability of all sites apply. No generic 21-day repeating calendar.

Distinct renal-source restrictions require specialist/pharmacy reconciliation: NCCP recommends creatinine clearance ≥50 mL/min before high-dose methotrexate, while its complication section prohibits treatment below an indexed 70 mL/min/1.73 m² and its renal-toxicity row contains a problematic ≥50 sign. Current HPRA high-dose methotrexate product information additionally contraindicates treatment at unindexed creatinine clearance below 60 mL/min (sections 4.2/4.3: https://assets.hpra.ie/products/Human/22092/Licence_PA0822-206-007_11092026121412.pdf). Do not equate or convert indexed and unindexed thresholds; these are not a patient dose or rescue calculator.

Source methotrexate hydration and rescue stopping thresholds differ (0.1 versus 0.15 micromol/L), a printed molar exponent is inconsistent, and the postoperative 11-dose/84-hour alternative must not stop rescue during delayed clearance. No automated rescue/discharge rule is provided.
All rescue clocks start at methotrexate infusion commencement, not completion. Rescue-table interval overlaps and the alternative formula require specialist/pharmacy adjudication.

Planned standard-course arithmetic: doxorubicin 450 mg/m², cisplatin 480 mg/m² and twelve methotrexate administrations; optional delay doses are separate. Prior anthracycline exposure and cardiac risk remain relevant.
Dose-modification source gaps, exact cardiac boundary and historical toxicity must be reviewed. No numerical dose modification or rescue calculator is authorised.

Doxorubicin product information recommends baseline cardiac imaging and repeats at approximately each accumulated 100 mg/m², more explicit than the NCCP conditional-imaging paragraph. Use a reconciled specialist cardiac plan; the source age>65 phrase must not imply younger patients need no cardiac monitoring.

medicines.dose: Prescribed and reconciled by the specialist team
medicines.timing: The prescription specifies treatment-day, delayed and rescue support

additional_support: Mifamurtide has moderate nausea/vomiting risk. Agree an individual anti-sickness plan without automatically adding routine dexamethasone or chronic steroids, which may oppose immune-cell activation. Paracetamol or an antihistamine may be prescribed for infusion symptoms; adult examples are not paediatric doses. Preventive inhaler treatment may be considered for asthma or chronic obstructive lung disease.

Confirm complete removal of all visible tumour, nonmetastatic eligibility and recovery from surgery. Calcineurin inhibitors such as ciclosporin and high-dose nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory painkillers must not be combined with mifamurtide. Check with oncology or the pharmacist before taking, starting, changing or stopping any medicine, including over-the-counter products; do not stop prescribed medicines yourself. Routine or chronic corticosteroids should be avoided, but emergency use is a separate medical decision. Any premedication requires an individual prescription, especially for a child. Arrange the separate 36-week treatment record.

The team chooses appropriate intravenous access and explains its care. Report pain, burning, redness or swelling during treatment immediately. If a port or peripherally inserted central catheter is used, confirm dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Never change pump settings or disconnect an infusion yourself.

Neurological management depends on current symptoms, severity, previous occurrences and documented recovery. Re-exposure, methylene blue or substitution requires a new specialist decision; none is automatically prescribed.
Ifosfamide kidney clearance below 50 mL/min or dialysis is a clinical decision, not an imported absolute rule from another regimen. Severe liver impairment is not recommended.

Identify the actual supplied ifosfamide product and reconcile its current product information with the exact NCCP regimen before administration or restart. The reviewed HPRA Mitoxana 1 g product (PA2299/028/001; 11 September 2023) lists serum creatinine above 120 micromol/L, bilirubin above 17 micromol/L, or transaminases/alkaline phosphatase above 2.5 times the local upper limit of normal as contraindications. These named-product restrictions are more restrictive than parts of the NCCP dose-modification tables. Do not use a national reference dose band or an approval checkbox to override a known supplied-product contraindication. An unknown or different product requires identification and oncology/pharmacy reconciliation; these thresholds must not silently become universal ifosfamide rules or replacement doses. Creatinine clearance is not serum creatinine, and a raw liver-enzyme value requires its actual local reference range.

Current ifosfamide central nervous system toxicity requires interruption and immediate clinical assessment. A broad neurological grade alone does not establish encephalopathy: distinguish central/brain symptoms from peripheral symptoms, and review unresolved localisation. Recovery of a current value does not erase prior severe toxicity, prior discontinuation or the source-specific requirements for any future rechallenge.
